_policyBundleNote: Optional. Set "policyBundle" to {"path": "<org bundle>.json", "lockfile": "<org bundle>.lock"} to take an org baseline from a content-addressed bundle (see bridge_policy_bundle.example.json). The host applies it only when its sha256 matches the lockfile, and this local file still layers on top and can only tighten. Leave it null to use this file as the sole policy source.

default._auditExportNote: Optional SIEM forwarder for audit events that were ALREADY written to the local log; the local log stays the source of truth. Set "auditExport" to {"format": "jsonl|syslog|cef", "destination": "<file path>" or "udp://host:port" or "tcp://host:port" or "<unix datagram socket>", "rotateBytes": <positive int>, "retainDays": <positive number>}. rotateBytes/retainDays apply to file destinations only. Anything malformed disables export after one audit_export_unavailable event; so does a sink that refuses a write. Test a destination first with: chrome-bridge audit export --format cef --destination /tmp/probe.cef --limit 5

default._dlpNote: Data-loss-prevention channel modes: allow (default), audit (permit and record one dlp_audit event naming the channel), block (deny with reason 'dlp blocked' before anything is forwarded). Enforced host-side at the chokepoints the bridge owns: upload gates uploadFile/githubAttachUploadedFiles/githubAttachPrBody, download gates downloadUrl, screenShare gates startScreencast/screencastFrames. 'clipboard' is a declared channel with NO chokepoint - no bridge action reads or writes the clipboard and a page-driven copy never crosses the bridge - so setting it records intent and enforces nothing. It is deliberately omitted here rather than listed as if it were covered.
